q: 176. A relatively fixed point of known elevation above datum is called
explain: A Bench Mark (BM) is a permanent point of reference whose elevation with respect to a specific datum is known and used for leveling operations.

q: 177. An operation for determining the relative elevations of different points on the surface of the earth is known as
explain: Differential leveling is the method used to determine the difference in elevation between two points, regardless of the distance between them.

q: 178. In a dumpy level, the objective and eyepiece lenses are made of two or more small lenses to obtain
explain: Composite lenses are used to correct aberrations (chromatic and spherical), resulting in a sharp, distinct image and better light transmission.

q: 179. The types of level normally used in hilly area is
explain: The Abney level is a handheld clinometer used to measure slopes and vertical angles, making it ideal for steep, hilly terrain.

q: 180. During levelling generally instrumental error is occuring due to
explain: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not truly horizontal even when the bubble is centered, which is a classic instrumental error.

q: 181. When bubble of the telescope is centered then
explain: In a perfectly adjusted level, centering the bubble ensures that the line of sight (axis of collimation) is truly horizontal.

q: 182. The image of the objectives formed should lie
options: in the plane of cross hairs
at the center of the eyepiece
at the optical center of the eyepiece.
explain: To eliminate parallax and take accurate readings, the image formed by the objective lens must coincide exactly with the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 183. The absence of spherical aberration in a telescope is known as
explain: Aplanatism (or aplanation) refers to a lens system that is free from both spherical aberration and coma.

q: 184. The absence of chromatic aberration in a telescope is known as
explain: Achromatism is the property of an optical system that eliminates chromatic aberration, allowing different wavelengths of light to focus at the same point.

q: 185. The magnification of a telescope depends upon
options: inverse of ratio of (b) and (a) above
explain: Magnifying power is defined by the ratio of the focal length of the objective ($f_o$) to the focal length of the eyepiece ($f_e$).

q: 186. In an internal focussing type of telescope, the negative lens provided is
explain: Internal focusing telescopes use a movable double concave (negative) lens located between the objective and the diaphragm.

q: 187. An inter focusing type of telescope is focused by the movement of
explain: In internal focusing, the objective and eyepiece remain fixed while a negative (concave) lens moves along the axis to focus.

q: 188. The sensitivity of the bubble tube can be increased by
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
increasing the diameter of the tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with an increase in the radius of curvature, the length of the bubble, and the internal diameter of the tube.

q: 189. A level tube is used to make line of sight horizontal. It is filled with
explain: Liquids like ether, alcohol, or chloroform are used because they have low viscosity and low freezing points, allowing the bubble to move quickly and freely.

q: 190. In a constant level tube, size of the bubble remains constant because upper wall of tube has
explain: A large radius of curvature in the upper wall allows for a more sensitive and stable bubble length despite minor temperature changes.

q: 191. If temperature increases the sensitivity of a bubble tube
explain: Increased temperature causes the liquid to expand, which decreases the length of the bubble and consequently its sensitivity.

q: 192. Sensitivity of a level tube is expressed by
options: length of bubble of level tube
explain: Sensitivity is mathematically related to the radius of curvature (R); the larger the radius, the more sensitive the tube.

q: 193. Dumpy level is used when
options: number of observation to be taken are large from one level position
number of observation to be taken are small from one level position
fly levelling is to be done
explain: Because the telescope is fixed to its supports, the Dumpy level is sturdy and efficient for taking many readings from a single setup.

q: 194. Automatic level has advantages of
options: freedom from errors and external influence
comfortable and has large range of application
explain: Automatic levels use a compensator to maintain a horizontal line of sight, making them faster, more precise, and more reliable than manual levels.

q: 195. The height of instrument method is
explain: The HI (Height of Instrument) method requires fewer calculations per point than the Rise and Fall method, making it faster for large numbers of intermediate sights.

q: 196. Height of instrument method of levelling as compared to rise and fall method is
explain: While less accurate in terms of self-checking intermediate sights, the HI method is significantly faster and easier to calculate.

q: 197. The rise and fall method of levelling provides a complete check on
explain: The Rise and Fall method has the advantage of checking all readings, including intermediate sights, ensuring the RL of every point is correct.

q: 198. The rise and fall method
options: provides a check on the intermediate readings
is preferable for differential and check levelling
explain: Due to its rigorous checking of all staff readings, it is the preferred method for high-precision engineering surveys.

q: 199. If the observed reading of a level staff is 3.83 m, and at the point sighted the staff is 0.15 m off the vertical through the bottom, the correct reading will be
explain: Using the Pythagorean theorem, the true vertical height is $\sqrt{3.83^2 - 0.15^2} \approx 3.827$ m.

q: 200. The observed reading on a levelling staff was 3.545 m. If the staff was 0.150 m off from the original ground level, what should be correct reading?
explain: If the staff is held 0.150m away/down from the original point, the reading must be adjusted by subtraction (3.545 - 0.150 = 3.395m) to reflect the correct ground position.

q: 201. The observed reading on a levelling staff was 3.525 m. If the staff was 0.125m on from the original ground level, what should be correct reading?
explain: If the staff is on (elevated) by 0.125m, the ground reading is calculated by adding the offset: 3.525 + 0.125 = 3.65m.

q: 202. The levelling of instrument is done such that
options: line of sight is truly horizontal
line of collimation is truly horizontal
explain: The fundamental purpose of leveling the instrument base is to ensure the vertical axis is truly vertical, which allows the line of sight to sweep a horizontal plane.

q: 203. In case of leveling staff readings are taken by (In case of target staff)
explain: In target leveling, the instrument man signals the staff man to move the target; once aligned, the staff man reads the value from the staff.

q: 204. Instrumental error in levelling is error due to
explain: All mentioned factors—lack of adjustment, poor bubble response, and loose mechanical parts—are categorized as instrumental errors.

q: 205. Natural error in levelling is caused due to
explain: Natural errors arise from environmental conditions like wind, heat (shimmer), and the earth's curvature/refraction.

q: 206. Permanent adjustment are carried out to
options: establish a fixed relationship between its fundamental axes
explain: Permanent adjustments ensure that the line of collimation, bubble axis, and vertical axis remain in their correct relative geometric positions.

q: 207. The line of collimation should be parallel to
explain: For the line of sight to be horizontal when the bubble is centered, the line of collimation must be parallel to the axis of the bubble tube.

q: 208. For Y level, Cooke's and Cushing levels, the line of collimation should coincide with
explain: In these specific types of levels, the mechanical design requires the line of collimation to coincide exactly with the optical axis of the telescope.

q: 209. In dumpy level in perfect adjustment, the horizontal cross hair should be in a plane
options: parallel to the axis of bubble tube
explain: The horizontal cross-hair must be perpendicular to the vertical axis so that it remains truly horizontal as the telescope is rotated.

q: 210. The two peg method is used to check the parallelism between the
options: line of collimation and axis of bubble tube
line of collimation and axis of telescope
axis of bubble tube and vertical axis
explain: The Two-Peg Test is the standard procedure to check for collimation error by ensuring the line of sight is parallel to the bubble tube axis.

q: 211. When it is not possible to set up the level, midway between the two points, then the difference in elevation between them is measured by
explain: Reciprocal leveling is used to eliminate curvature, refraction, and collimation errors when points are separated by an obstacle like a river where no middle setup is possible.

q: 212. The method of levelling used to carry out the reconnaissance of area is
explain: Fly leveling is a rapid method of leveling used to establish approximate elevations or to connect a benchmark to a starting point during reconnaissance.

q: 213. The accuracy required in precise levelling is of the order of
options: all of the above (Where K is total distance)
explain: Depending on the class of precision (First, Second, or Third order), the error limits are typically defined as a multiple of the square root of the distance $K$ in kilometers.

q: 214. The levels to which the earthwork will have to be carried out is known as
explain: The formation level is the final intended elevation of the ground surface after excavation or embankment is completed.

q: 215. If the formation level is less than the ground level, the difference between them at any point will give the
explain: When the design level (formation) is below the existing ground surface, you must 'cut' or excavate soil to reach it.

q: 216. The reciprocal levelling eliminates
options: the error due to curvature and refraction
explain: By taking readings from both ends of the line, reciprocal leveling cancels out the combined effects of curvature, refraction, and any residual collimation error.

q: 217. Due to curvature of the earth object looks
explain: Earth's curvature causes the level line to fall away from the horizontal tangent, making objects appear lower than their true elevation.

q: 218. The correction for refraction is given by
explain: The refraction correction ($C_r$) is approximately $1/7$ of the curvature correction, calculated as $0.0112 d^2$ where $d$ is the distance in km.

q: 219. If the distance between two points A and B is 1km, the combined correction for curvature and refraction will be
explain: The combined correction ($C$) is calculated as $C = 0.0673 d^2$. For $d = 1$ km, $C = 0.0673$ m.

q: 220. The sensitivity of the bubble tube expressed in terms of angular value of one division of the bubble is given by
explain: Sensitivity $\alpha = s / (nD)$, where $s$ is the total staff intercept and $D$ is the distance; for one division, it is expressed as $s/D$ radians.

q: 221. Personal error in levelling occur due to
explain: Personal errors are caused by the surveyor's limitations or negligence, such as improper leveling or misreading the staff.

q: 222. Levelling across a river is done by
explain: Reciprocal leveling is specifically designed for situations where a large distance (like a river) prevents the level from being placed in the center.

q: 223. In trigonometrical levelling the combined correction is given by
explain: In higher-level surveying, the combined correction formula includes the coefficient of refraction ($m$) and earth's radius ($R$).

q: 224. Bench marks are fixed by
explain: Spirit leveling (using a level and staff) is the most accurate method and is used for establishing permanent Bench Marks.

q: 225. The last reading of levelling is always a
explain: A leveling circuit or run always concludes with a Fore Sight (FS) on a point of known or final elevation.

q: 226. The first reading of leveling is always
explain: Every leveling operation must start with a Back Sight (BS) taken on a point of known elevation (Bench Mark) to establish the Height of Instrument.

q: 227. The first reading taken at turning point is
explain: At a turning point (change point), a Fore Sight is taken to find the point's elevation, and then the first reading after moving the instrument is a Back Sight to continue the line.

q: 228. If the BM of a station A is 500 m. The back sight reading at the point A is 2 m and fore sight reading of station B is 3 m, then find the RL of station B
explain: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL + BS = 500 + 2 = 502 m. RL of B = HI - FS = 502 - 3 = 499 m.

q: 229. The RL of BM is 1000.00 m. Back sight reading at the BM is 2.555 and RL of IS is 1000.055 then find the reading of IS
230. Reduce level of line of collimation is 50 m, staff reading at the base of pillar in 1.15 m then find the reduce level of base of pillar
explain: RL of point = RL of Collimation (HI) - Staff Reading = 50 - 1.15 = 48.85 m.

q: 231. The Bench Mark of a point is 400m. Back sight reading at bench mark is 2.20 and fore sight reading of point A is 2.10 then find the RL of the point A
232. Find the RL of collimation line if the RL of BM is 100 m & BS staff reading is 5.35 m
explain: The Reduced Level of the collimation line is simply the Height of Instrument (HI), which is RL + BS = 100 + 5.35 = 105.35 m.

q: 233. The elevation (BM) of point A is 100 m. Back sight reading at A is 20 and fore sight reading at B is 30 m. Find the RL of point B
234. Tilting levels are used for
explain: Tilting levels are designed for high precision because the line of sight can be adjusted slightly for each reading to be perfectly horizontal.

q: 235. The types of survey used for Geodetic survey is
explain: Geodetic surveys cover large areas and require extreme accuracy to account for earth's curvature, necessitating precise leveling methods.

q: 236. Compensator is used to make the line of sight perpendicular to vertical axis in case of
explain: An automatic level contains a compensator (an optical pendulum) that automatically levels the line of sight even if the telescope is slightly tilted.

q: 237. In leveling across a hill, the level should be set up on
explain: When leveling up or down a slope, the instrument is placed on the side of the hill in a 'zigzag' pattern to maintain a manageable staff height.

q: 238. Level surface is parallel to
explain: A level surface is a curved surface that is at all points normal to the direction of gravity. It is not parallel to a flat horizontal surface.

q: 239. The surface perpendicular to the direction of the gravity is
explain: By definition, a level surface (like the mean surface of a still lake) is always perpendicular to the local plumb line (direction of gravity).

q: 240. The Philadelphia rod is a type of
explain: The Philadelphia rod is a two-section telescopic leveling staff that can be extended for higher readings.

q: 241. The correction for curvature as applied to staff reading is
explain: Curvature correction ($C_c$) is always subtractive from the staff reading because the earth curves away from the horizontal line. Formula: $-d^2/2R$.

q: 242. The curvature and refraction corrections applied to staff readings respectively are
explain: Curvature correction is negative (subtractive) while refraction correction is positive (additive) to the staff reading.

q: 243. If the level tube is out of adjustment by an angle e, when the telescope is rotated through 180°, it becomes
explain: Rotating the telescope by 180° doubles the angular error relative to the vertical axis, hence 2e.

q: 244. Line of collimation is
options: is the same line of sight
the line joining point of intersection of cross hairs and optical centre of object glass
the geometrical axis of the telescope
the line parallel to the bubble tube axis
explain: The line of collimation is the specific line of sight defined by the cross-hair intersection and the optical center of the objective lens.

q: 245. Pick up the odd statement
options: temporary adjustment of Dumpy level are to be performed at every set up
the eye piece need not be adjusted after the first set up when the same surveyor is taking readings
parallax error is completely eliminated when there is no change in the staff reading when the eye is moved up and down
focus the objective towards a white or bright background for the clear visibility of cross hairs
explain: Option (d) is odd because you focus the *eyepiece* (not the objective) against a white background to see the cross-hairs clearly.

q: 246. "Cross-sectioning" and "Longitudinal sectioning" is
options: when less number of intermediate sight exist
explain: Profile leveling involves taking readings along a center line (longitudinal) and at right angles to it (cross-sectioning) to map the terrain.

q: 247. An invert is taken when the point is
options: above the line of the sight
explain: An 'inverted staff' reading is taken when the point (like the underside of a bridge or ceiling) is higher than the instrument's line of sight.

q: 248. Ten readings were recorded in a level field book. If the instrument was shifted after 2nd and 6th readings, then the fore sight are
explain: The reading taken immediately before a shift is a Fore Sight. Additionally, the final reading of any run is always a Fore Sight. Thus: 2nd, 6th, and 10th.

q: 249. Fifteen readings were recorded in a level field book. If the instrument was shifted after 5th, 10th and 15th readings, then the fore sights are
explain: Similar to the previous logic, shift readings and the final reading are Fore Sights: 5th, 10th, and 15th.

q: 250. In profile levelling, staff readings on two neighboring pegs 20 m apart are 1.20 and 1.00 respectively. Therefore, the proposed road had a
explain: Difference in level = 1.20 - 1.00 = 0.20 m (rise). Gradient = Rise/Distance = 0.20/20 = 1/100. Since the reading decreased, the ground rose.
